name: non-mechanical back and neck pain overview
title: Non-mechanical back and neck pain: a nerve squeezed at the side (radiculopathy) or in the centre (lumbar stenosis, cauda equina syndrome, cervical myelopathy), or everything else flagged by red flags (inflammatory, fracture, infection or neoplasm); each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment, with visceral causes and the no-red-flag starting treatment below

root.title: Back or neck pain that is NOT just mechanical: where is the problem?
lines: OLDCARS + red flags every time · first exclude non-spinal causes: hip, visceral, vascular, systemic, viral
nerve compression can come from ANYTHING: disc, spondylosis, abscess, tumour, bleed, slipped vertebra

groups.title: To the SIDE: a ROOT
lines: in or around the neural foramen

groups.title: In the CENTRE: canal stenosis
lines: the cord ends at ~L1: lumbar stenosis squeezes ROOTS, cervical squeezes the CORD

groups.title: EVERYTHING ELSE: found by red flags
lines: red flag → plain films for fracture · MRI for neurological compromise, infection, neoplasm

head: h
Radiculopathy
degenerative (disc, spondylosis) by far the commonest
pres: • EASED by slackening the nerve: arm overhead, legs curled
The disc hits the LOWER root
inv: image if the deficit is severe or progressing
• neck: neurological signs, or pain > 4 weeks of conservative care
• X-ray NOT indicated · EMG tests the root
tx: • excellent prognosis: most settle over months
• SHORT opioid course if pain is severe

head: h
Lumbar central stenosis
squeezes ROOTS
pres: • NEUROGENIC CLAUDICATION: worse walking a distance
• eased by flexion: grocery cart, uphill, sitting (slower than vascular)

head: h
Cauda equina syndrome
the severe end of lumbar stenosis
tx: decompress within 48 h of onset: much better outcomes

head: h
Cervical myelopathy
central stenosis squeezes the CORD
pres: • UPPER motor neuron signs below the level
hard to squeeze the cord and miss a root

head: h
Inflammatory
seronegative spondyloarthropathy: ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic, IBD, reactive
pres: • night pain, 2nd half of the night
tx: treatment comes in the rheumatology lectures

head: h
Fracture
fall or trauma · osteoporosis · past fragility fracture
pres: elderly, on steroids · minor or NO trauma · axial pain with radiation
young athletes who EXTEND: gymnasts, football, weightlifters

head: h
Infection · Neoplasm
osteomyelitis, discitis, epidural abscess · bone tumour, mass, drop metastases
pres: • young · severe night pain · weight loss, night sweats
tx: tumour or large abscess on a nerve → decompression

panels.title: No red flags: start here (radicular, stenosis, non-specific)
items: advice + reassurance: good prognosis, NO immediate imaging
radicular pain: exercise, physiotherapy · neuropathic agents · opioids for rescue
acute non-specific: STAY ACTIVE, no bed rest · physiotherapy · NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, weak opioids
persistent non-specific: exercise, psychological therapies, multidisciplinary care · NSAIDs with caution

panels.title: Visceral pain felt in the back
items: abdominal aortic aneurysm: pulsatile mass · vertebral artery insufficiency: dizziness, cranial nerve findings · atypical cardiac
GI: peptic ulcer, pancreatitis · GU: pyelonephritis, kidney stones, endometriosis
